text.p: Bangladesh Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said the country's sick industries unable to survive on their own would be liquidated.
"We will try ... to rehabilitate those sick industries which have potential, but if the efforts fail they will be liquidated," Kibria told a meeting of businessmen on Sunday.
He blamed the failure of management, which he said caused huge defaulted loans with the commercial banks.

"The commercial banks are struggling to realise these huge defaulted loans. But the entrepreneurs refused to pay back the loans on the grounds of the sickness of their industries," Kibria said. Kibria said the government would speed up import liberalisation in future after allowing some breathing space for domestic industries in fiscal 1997/98 (July-June).
"The government has slowed the trade liberalisation in this year's budget only to allow the local industry to be equipped to compete globally," he said.
Kibria said the government had given the sick industries enough concessions by exempting interest on loans and providing other incentives.
"The culture of interest exemption must go. For every debt forgiven there is a liability created," the minister said.
"The borrowers who pay regularly will be rewarded by way of rebate," he added.
